macrostructure: Split Monitor (the engagement split), nested in an editorial Ledger — with a Question Board opening the home page
screen: en|th marketing site — full copy and route rewrite across home, services, about, contact
notes: Second entry for the MARKETING site, whose system is the Engineering Field Guide block at assets/site.css:1 (paper/ink/teal, borders-only) and NOT the .interface-design/system.md at this directory, which governs the TCO calculator's dark violet/cyan panel — the same trap the 2026-09-11 and the quotes entry both record, checked and refused again. S9 is satisfied without a justified repeat: the previous entry is Workbench/Ledger/Stacked Sections and the previous entry for THIS site is Topology. Shape argument: the home page had a linear 'progression' strip that narrated a process nobody asked about. It is replaced by three shapes that each answer one question. (1) A Question Board opens the page, because the argument of the offer is that four specific questions get settled during design rather than discovered in production, so the QUESTIONS must be the loudest thing in the section — they are the h3, with a mono ? in the gutter, not cards with headings. (2) The engagement section is a Split Monitor and is the signature move of this build: two halves, direct client and partner subcontract, with ONE shared question printed above both marks — who holds the customer relationship — so the DIFFERENCE is what the reader sees rather than two panels that happen to sit side by side, which is precisely the shape's Must-not-become clause. The density floor for a Split Monitor is symmetry, and .route-mark{margin-top:auto} in a flex column is what holds it: both marks sit on one line regardless of how long either body runs, so asymmetry cannot creep in through copy edits. (3) The process section is a numbered two-up, deliberately quiet and last, because process is reassurance and not the pitch. Routes collapsed 7 to 4 on operator decision (home, services, about, contact); /platform/, /governance/ and /how-we-work/ are RETIRED but not deleted — this is GitHub Pages with no server-side redirect capability and those URLs are indexed, so each of the six en|th files is now a hand-written meta-refresh stub carrying rel=canonical, noindex/follow and a visible fallback link, marked in a header comment as not generated by scripts/build-site.mjs. The Light product framing was demoted to evidence rather than deleted: the hero topology figure stays but its boundary label is now GOVERNED EXECUTION with the branding removed, and the approval-gate demo moved from the retired /governance/ into the services page's AI-governance block. Three section kinds were added to the allow-list in scripts/build-site.mjs (questions, routes, process) and three were deleted with their CSS (progression, flow, governance-teaser); .flowchart and its node states were deliberately PRESERVED because the demo survived the page that hosted it. site/config.mjs identity strings were frozen on purpose: tests/website.test.mjs:86-91 byte-asserts organizationDescription against the JSON-LD inside light-tools.html, so editing it would silently pull light-tools.html and tco-calculator.html into the blast radius of a copy change. The architect bio retains 'nearly 20 years', the founder title and the Red Hat/Nutanix history at the operator's explicit instruction, which was taken after flagging that docs/service-offer-spec.md section 8 bars those as unverified; that is a recorded operator decision about their own background, not an oversight. Gates 54/54, 0 unresolved failures, with 7 argued and 5 not applicable enumerated in the stamp rather than silently passed — V3 Inter (Latin half of a bilingual pairing), V4 the --focus hue (pre-existing semantic status token, reused for refusal), V6 radius literals (3px buttons, 2px inputs, pre-existing and untokenised), V10/V11 pre-existing spacing drift and the styled native select, and T1/T3 loading (nothing on this site is async: the contact form composes a mailto draft in-page and the demo is a local simulation). One near-miss is recorded rather than hidden: .ledger and .exceptions now share the index + split-body skeleton and a THIRD kind on that skeleton would fail S3; they currently stay distinct on column ratio, rule direction and heading scale. Critique H4 D5 S4 O5 R4 P4. Measurement honesty: light_browser verb:eval remains unavailable in this environment, so the numbers come from the repo's own tests/website-browser-check.html fixture, which reported PASS across 24 layout cases (4 routes x 2 locales x 390/768/1440) with minContrast 5.46 and no overflow. The EN home page was screenshotted and looked at; the TH home page was NOT — background-tab capture timed out twice against the headed host client — so every Thai claim in this entry is a MEASUREMENT from the fixture and not a look, and the new html[lang=th] .route-mark span override is therefore verified as passing layout rather than judged for composition. The instrument lied once and it is worth carrying forward: tests/website-browser-check.html:44 asserted a hard-coded nav count of 7, so collapsing the routes turned a correct site into eight false 'mobile navigation incomplete' failures at 390 and 768 while 1440 stayed clean. It now asserts the invariant — every nav link is visible once the menu opens — because a fixture that hard-codes a number from the contract becomes a liar the moment the contract changes. Next revision on this site should not reach for Split Monitor again without stating why, and must keep the shared question above the two marks: the moment the halves stop answering one question about two subjects, the shape is wrong.

macrostructure: Workbench (quotations, clients, invoices) · Ledger (catalog, and nested in every detail pane) · Stacked Sections (reports, settings)
depth: borders-only — one exception, the confirm dialog's scrim
screen: quotes/ui — all 8 operator screens (quotations list + detail, clients, catalog, invoices list + detail, reports, settings)
notes: First entry for the QUOTES app, which is a different product from the marketing site and the TCO calculator that fill the rest of this log — so there is no prior shape to diversify against, and the Command Deck attractor was rejected on the brief rather than on repetition: the job is working one record to a decision, not monitoring at a glance. The three summary figures that would have been its KPI cards are a single ruled Position strip, reordered BELOW the list on a phone. This app has its own system at quotes/.interface-design/system.md; the system.md at THIS directory governs the TCO calculator's dark violet/cyan panel and was deliberately not applied — the same trap the 2026-09-11 entry records. Gates 51/54, with three exceptions argued rather than passed silently. T5 (a list with no pagination, virtualisation or stated cap) is OPEN and genuinely unmet: GET /quotations returns every row and the rail renders all of them, which is correct at this business's volume but is not a cap; closing it needs either 'showing first 200 of N' in .rail-count or a real window in workbench.js, and it is filed as a todo. N2 (Ledger row above 48px) is ACCEPTED because it is in direct arithmetic conflict with A4: the catalog row carries three inline controls, and a 36px control inside 8+8 padding and a 1px rule is 61px, while raising those controls to A4's 44px makes the row 69px and shrinking the row under 48px puts the controls under 32px. Two gates in one rubric cannot both hold for a row with inline actions; this build resolved toward the target size. A4 (targets below 44x44) is ACCEPTED at a measured 36px minimum — every primary control is 44px, and the exceptions are button.sm on catalog and inline-edit rows plus the 40px rail-head search, all of which exist to hold the density floors N1-N3 demands. WCAG 2.2 AA (2.5.8) asks 24x24; 44x44 is 2.5.5, which is AAA, and the harness reports the AA and AAA counts separately so this can never read as a pass. Critique H4 D4 S4 O5 R4 P4 — specificity is 4 rather than 5 because a Workbench is a well-known shape; what another model would not have produced from this brief is the status encoding that survives greyscale (colour AND border style on the rail's left edge), a delete rule keyed to invoice EXISTENCE rather than to status, and the Position strip demoted below the records on a phone. Measured across 8 screens x 390/768/1440, 0 fail, via quotes/tests/ui-harness.html served by tests/ui-harness-server.mjs. Two measurement constraints worth carrying forward: light_browser verb:eval is unavailable in this environment, so the measurement runs in-page and is read back as a text snapshot; and Chrome CORS-blocks ES module imports from a file:// origin, so these screens CANNOT be measured off disk at all and the loopback harness is mandatory rather than a convenience — it also means every measurement exercises the real API transport instead of a stub. Five apparent UI failures this round were bugs in the INSTRUMENT, not the screens (an ellipsised rail name charged as clipped content, .totals summary rows counted as Ledger rows, the harness's own fixture banner inflating the fold measurement, and the 12-row rail floor applied at single-column widths where the rail's box is its own content height); each fix carries its reason in ui-harness.html so it cannot be simplified back. Looking caught what measuring could not: the rail's client names were justify-content:space-between, so a short name floated to the right edge and the column an operator scans down did not exist — no gate fires on that. Next product-UI build in this repo should not reach for Workbench again without stating why.

density: balanced — a five-node governance chain, readable at the default fit without zooming
screen: en|th /governance/ — the halting approval flowchart in the demo section
notes: First Topology entry in this log. Differs from the previous five (Focus Rail, Comparison Canvas with Conversation, Decision Ledger, Spec-Sheet Ledger x2) on shape, so the S9 diversification rule is satisfied without needing a justified repeat. This governs the MARKETING site, whose system is the Engineering Field Guide block at assets/site.css:1 (paper/ink/teal, borders-only) — NOT the .interface-design/system.md at the repo root, which governs the TCO Calculator's dark violet/cyan instrument panel. Applying the root system's tokens here would have been the trap; it was checked and refused. The operator asked for a flowchart that stops and waits for a human and then continues to the end once approved, so the chain is the argument of the page rather than decoration: evaluate paints pass,pass,deny,wait,idle and STOPS at stage 04, and approve paints all five pass. Signature move honoured — each node carries its state as a glyph (check/cross/dot/middot) AND a border weight (1/2/3px) AND a colour, so it survives greyscale and colour-blindness; the Must-not-become clause is honoured because the chart is a server-rendered <ol> on fixed grid columns and JS mutates only data-state, never order or position, so layout is byte-identical on every load. The always-visible legend is a real element, not a hover tooltip. Accessibility split: the chart itself is aria-hidden and decorative, while .demo-status is the role=status live region that announces every transition in words, and .static-explanation carries the entire argument with JavaScript switched off. Motion: node transitions are 220ms on border-color/background-color only (never layout properties), staged 260ms apart; prefers-reduced-motion is handled twice over — assets/site.css:15 kills all animation and transition globally, and bindDemo detects it in JS and applies the identical END state with zero staging, so nothing is lost with motion off. Gates 54/54 after adding the stamp; S1 was the one genuine failure (no macrostructure named) and is now fixed. Four argued exceptions are recorded in the stamp rather than silently passed: V3 Inter (deliberate Latin half of a bilingual pairing with Noto Sans Thai), V4 second hue (--focus is the pre-existing semantic status token, reused not introduced), V10 and V11 (pre-existing site spacing drift and the native select, both outside this change). Critique H4 D4 S4 O5 R4 P4. Measurement honesty: light_browser verb:eval is REFUSED on the credentialed host client and the operator client is offline, so no computed-style snippet was run this round — the numbers come instead from the repo's own tests/website-browser-check.html fixture, which measures in iframes at 390/768/1440 and reported PASS across 42 layout cases with minContrast 5.46 and no overflow; composition and hierarchy claims come from screenshots. One defect the rendered screen caught that code review did not: the demo.approved copy still said 'run the request again to continue' while the chart already showed the execute node passed, so picture and text contradicted each other; the string was rewritten in both locales. Next revision on this site should not reach for Topology again without stating why, and should avoid letting status copy and chart state drift apart — they are now two renderings of one model and must move together.

screen: tco-calculator.html v0.8 — input rail restructured around decisions; conversational assist thread on the interview step
notes: Fifth tco-calculator entry and a macrostructure change to the RAIL specifically; the Guided Stepper beside it is unchanged and still governs the top of the column. The previous rail shape was 'noun-grouped field vault with nested disclosure' — six sections named for categories of field (Who uses it, Hardware & prices, Money), three of which arrived folded, and inside two of those a SECOND <details class='adv'>. Routing policy was therefore two disclosures deep, which is exactly the 'buried' complaint. Three changes. (1) Sections are named for the decision they settle, not the fields they hold: How much demand / What the work is / Which model you'd run / What you'd compare against / What you assume about money / Service level & routing, each with the question restated in its hint. (2) One disclosure layer. 'Service level, routing & overlay' (12 fields) was PROMOTED out of Money into its own top-level section — it is not a money assumption, it is the separate decision of what happens when local capacity runs out. 'Architecture detail' (4 fields) became a labelled band (.subsec) inside the model section, because it is the shape of the model chosen above rather than a decision of its own. 'Tokens per turn' KEEPS its <details>: it is a 4x4 table of 16 raw inputs, not a decision, and unwrapping it would put bare numbers in the rail. (3) The fold defaults moved from a heading allow-list in fields.js (OPEN_SECTIONS) to `data-open` in the markup — the old coupling meant renaming a heading silently folded every section, and this revision renamed all six. A test now asserts both directions. Anti-slop on this diff: no new depth strategy, no colour literal outside the token block, no card grid, no icons, no invented number, no new interactive element needing states. .subsec deliberately does NOT get an uppercase mono micro-label: system.md rations those to one per section spine, so the band caption is 11.5px sans in --dim over a hairline. Verified in the server-hosted Chrome at 1920: all seven sections render, the three data-open sections arrive expanded and the other four folded with live value summaries, and the promoted section carries its own summary. eval is unavailable on that browser client, so contrast, 44px targets and narrow-viewport behaviour are NOT pixel-measured this round — they are unchanged CSS from v0.7, which was measured at 390/1100/1920. Also in this revision: the assist ask box left <details class='ai-assist'> and now sits on the interview step with a per-question answer thread, and the vendor name is gone from every UI surface (retained in privacy.html and llms.txt as a disclosure). ADDED AFTER THE FIRST RAIL PASS: a revision preview (#ai-revision) in the answerbar, shown only when an answer has drifted from the applied snapshot. It borrows the .ai-proposal shape on purpose — both say 'here is what would change, and nothing has changed yet' — but takes the ACCENT border rather than cyan, because this is the visitor's own pending edit and not something the model proposed; the edited answer chip gets the same accent plus a small mono 'edited' marker. One thing the rendered screen caught that the code review did not: the block appeared below the fold. Changing an answer leaves the visitor at the top of a tall rail while the answerbar sits near its bottom, so a preview nobody scrolls to is the same as no preview; renderRevision now scrollIntoView({block:'nearest'}) on the hidden->visible transition ONLY, so re-renders never fight the visitor's own scrolling. Verified by screenshot at the Xvfb width: the panel, the Control/Now/Would become table and both buttons sit in the viewport after a chip edit. Still NOT pixel-measured this round (eval remains operator-only): contrast, 44px targets, and the 390/1100 widths. Next calculator revision should not add a third disclosure layer to the rail, and should get eval access so the narrow widths stop being carried forward as unmeasured.

screen: services.html v2 — repositioning revision, electric-yellow palette, reading mode
notes: S9 repeat is deliberate and justified: this is the SAME screen revised, not a new one, so the shape is held fixed and only the argument, palette and small-screen behaviour changed. Three substantive changes. (1) Reading mode: the fixed 1920x1080 stage letterboxed to a 390x219 strip on a phone with 2.6px micro-labels while the nav chrome stayed full size, so the deck read as broken when SENT AS A LINK — which is half its job. Below 1100px it now leaves the stage entirely and renders the same DOM as a scrolling document. This is a deliberate override of slide-design's 'letterbox, never reflow' invariant, which assumes a presentation-only artifact; the reading tier declares its own clamp-bounded fluid scale rather than the enumerated stage ladder (argued V10 + V13). (2) Palette: violet retired — it was borrowed from a vendor relationship that has ended — and replaced with electric yellow #FFE800 as the brand signal, cyan kept for link/data. --warn moved amber -> orange so the clock dot stays a separate semantic against the new accent. tco-calculator.html KEEPS violet; system.md still governs it. (3) Positioning: the deck stopped arguing against systems integrators. Slide 9 became two positive audience columns (infrastructure owner / delivery partner), slide 10 became three negotiable contract shapes with knowledge transfer as an explicit line item rather than an assumed default, and the close moved from 'your renewal date' to 'send me the part that is hard' so it lands for both audiences. Gates 47 pass / 7 argued / 0 unresolved; critique H4 D4 S3 O5 R4 P4. Next deck build should avoid Spec-Sheet Ledger without stating why.

macrostructure: Guided Stepper beside a Live Ledger
screen: tco-calculator.html v0.7 — eight-question guided interview, no credential UI, MiniMax as assistant not driver
notes: Third tco-calculator entry and a deliberate macrostructure CHANGE from yesterday's Conversation-led Cost Ledger: the blank composer was the wrong primary affordance, because an untrained visitor cannot know what the calculator needs to be told. The typed transcript is not deleted — it is demoted into a <details class='ai-assist'> below the stepper, which is where a free-form question still belongs. Restructured WITHIN system.md rather than redesigned: same dark instrument panel, same borders-only depth, same violet+cyan, same mono-for-values rule; nothing in the token layer changed. New components are a numbered 1..8 progress rail whose steps are themselves jump targets, option cards with a selected and a separate is-recommended state (violet marks the visitor's choice; the MiniMax suggestion gets its own quieter border plus an explicit 'MiniMax suggests this' label so advice can never be mistaken for a selection), inline numeric inputs on the three quantitative questions, and revisable answer chips under the stepper. Anti-slop: no wizard progress bar with a percentage, no card carousel, no stepper illustration, no gradient on the active step, no icon set — the rail is numbers and eyebrow words only. The riskiest surface here is the recommendation state; it was given a distinct treatment precisely because a 'suggested' option that looked selected would be an inert-boundary violation rendered in CSS. Verified in hosted Chrome at 390/1100/1920: no horizontal body overflow, all option/nav actions >=44px, contrast holds on the recommendation label. Next calculator revision should not add a third distinct AI surface without retiring one.
